title: Public ProxyException with a nested Kind enum, a status derived from the kind, a null message and one public constructor
Proxy path and request-target checks: dangerous raw paths answer 400 before any backend connection, and the target origin is pinned

title: Proxy.to(url) accepts an http or https origin with an optional base path, strips trailing slashes and rejects every other URL at the call
Proxy option values are checked at the option call: range errors and managed header names throw IllegalArgumentException, null throws NullPointerException
Proxy request header forwarding: received order and duplicates kept, hop-by-hop and Expect removed, Cookie lines merged, no Via, headers checked and written in ISO-8859-1
Proxy Host handling: Host becomes the target host unless preserveHost(true), the received Host goes to X-Forwarded-Host, and several Host lines answer 400
Proxy X-Forwarded-* trust rules: X-Forwarded-For appended only for a trusted peer, X-Forwarded-Proto from isSecure(), X-Forwarded-Host from the received Host, other forwarding headers dropped
Proxy fixed request headers: requestHeader replaces the client's same-name header, removeRequestHeader drops it, both apply last and the later call for a name wins
Proxy forwarded target: the base path followed by originalUrl() by default or by url() under stripPrefix(true), with method, path, query and body unchanged
Proxy request framing checks: ambiguous Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding answer 400 or 501 before any backend connection
Proxy request body framing to the backend: the length header is rewritten for the body actually sent, streamed without buffering, with a one-byte pre-read for requests without length headers
Proxy body limit and client body failures: bodyLimit or rawBodyLimit gives 413, read failures close the backend connection, a consumed body gives 500 without connecting
Proxy method handling: tokens forwarded as received, CONNECT and TRACE answered 405, WebSocket upgrades passed to next(), other upgrades forwarded without Upgrade, no next() after forwarding
Proxy check order and its own answers: one fixed order of checks before forwarding, with 400, 405 and 501 thrown as plain HttpException with a null message
